business_scope.primary_industry_name: Serialized Digital Web Fiction and Interactive Reading App

stage_1.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / certificate of good standing of corporate general partner (or its trust deed for an individual? no)
stage_1.issuing_entity: Competent company registrar / corporations registry in the partner's country of origin
stage_1.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1912? no—1961 Hague Convention) prior to consular authentication; for non-Hague member states, consular legalization at the Embassy/Consulate of Canada in the issuing state

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (C.C.Q.), arts. 2238-2264 (limited partnership) and Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c P-44.1), arts. 9-12
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Québec Enterprise Registrar
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de société en commandite (Declaration of Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no statutory escrow account requirement. Capital contributions are determined contractually and may consist of money, property, or personal service (limited partners cannot contribute service).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that upon the issuance of the attestation of registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the Limited Partnership is deemed constituted; that the capital contributions subscribed by the general and limited partners under the Partnership Agreement are accepted and credited; that the registered office of the Limited Partnership is established at [registered office address]; that [Name] is appointed as Chief Executive Officer and [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, register tax programs, and secure necessary permits; that all officers and partners are authorised to execute, acknowledge, and deliver all documents required to complete the formation of said Limited Partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online name search and reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary search in the Register of Enterprises for proposed names. File a name reservation application online or at a REQ service office. Confirm that the legal element 'société en commandite' or 'L.P.' is included. Pay the reservation fee or integrate it into the subsequent registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed legal name with required legal element
Three alternative names (optional)
Identification of the applicant general partner
Power of attorney if filed through a professional agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for confusion, submit an alternate name or obtain a letter of consent from the conflicting entity. If a prohibited term is used, amend the name and resubmit. The applicant may appeal the refusal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Capital Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties (partners) under the Civil Code of Québec; optional notarisation before a Quebec notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Receive and review the draft Limited Partnership Agreement. Ensure compliance with the French-language requirements of the Charter of the French Language. Execute two original copies with all partners, initial all schedules, and complete the capital contribution schedule in accordance with the agreed business terms.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement signed by all partners
Identification and residency proof of each general partner
Capital contribution schedule and proof of payment
Power of attorney if a partner is represented
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a partner refuses to execute, the non-consenting partner may be removed or replaced through an amendment. If the agreement contains a condition precedent that fails, the parties may rescind and new partners subscribe. For notarisation deficiencies, have the agreement restated and re-signed with corrected schedules.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Declaration of Limited Partnership with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – online registration portal (clicSÉQUR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the REQ online service, select 'société en commandite', and complete the déclaration. Provide legal name, registered office address, postal address, general partner details, business activity (ISIC 9000), and capital sum if requested. Attach the partnership agreement and proof of name attestation. Pay the publication fee and submit.
required_dossiers: Completed declaration on the REQ portal
Limited Partnership Agreement (PDF)
Name attestation confirmation
Registered office address proof (lease or deed)
Identification of general partners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The REQ issues a notice of deficiency allowing 30 days for correction. Correct the erroneous fields, resubmit, and retain the original priority date. Late corrections after default require a new application and may incur an additional $16 fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec (GST/QST), Canada Revenue Agency (GST/HST), Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the attested NEQ, register for provincial TVQ and QST and federal GST/HST accounts. If employees are anticipated, open a payroll account with Revenu Québec and register as an employer with CNESST. Complete any applicable beginning-of-business declaration, including revenue estimates and banking details.
required_dossiers: Attestation of NEQ registration
Revenue estimates to determine GST/QST registration thresholds
Bank account confirmation
Registered office address proof
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Penalties for late registration may be partially waived through a voluntary disclosure to Revenu Québec or CRA under the fairness provisions. If CNESST refuses an employer account because of incorrect SIN or address, verify and resubmit within 30 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Governance Initialisation and Registered Office Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and managing officers; REQ for any post-registration updates
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial meeting of the general partner. Adopt the first board resolution, record minutes, accept partnership interests, appoint officers, and open the partnership's bank account. Ensure the registered office is physically available and that a consent of the owner (or sublessor) is kept in the partnership records.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and signature page
Partnership minute book and register
Consent of owner for registered office
Bank account opening receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an officer refuses to sign, the general partner may appoint another by a supplementary resolution. Missing document filings are corrected by filing an amendment with REQ; late updates after 60 days trigger a late fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – the digital web novel platform is not a manufacturing, extractive, or industrial facility. Standard municipal permit only if physical offices are maintained.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – no sector-specific operating licence is imposed on online serial fiction subscription platforms in Quebec; REQ enterprise registration is the primary legal permit.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – the activity is purely digital; it does not trigger the provincial EIA review process for industrial plants or extractive operations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – no wastewater, volatile organic compound (VOC), or solid waste emissions are generated. Cloud hosting is subject to the vendor’s environmental management standards, not provincial discharge permits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For any physical office, obtain fire safety clearance from the municipal fire service and structural occupancy confirmation in accordance with the Building Act (CQLR c B-1.1). Workplace compliance is under the Act respecting occupational health and safety (CQLR c S-2.1); no civilian defence clearance is required for this digital activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), including the Business Registration Online service and My Business Account portal, for federal business numbers, GST/HST accounts, payroll and information-return accounts; and Revenu Québec, including the clicSÉQUR–Entreprises portal and My Account for Businesses, for Quebec sales tax (QST) registration, filings and payments. A Quebec limited partnership must also maintain its civil and enterprise-registration records with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), which is separate from tax registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Obtain or confirm the Quebec limited partnership's Québec enterprise number (NEQ) through the REQ. 2. Obtain a nine-digit CRA Business Number (BN) through CRA Business Registration Online, the CRA non-resident registration process, or an authorized representative; foreign partners may be required to provide formation documents, partnership agreement, registered-office information, responsible-person details and identity documentation. 3. Register the applicable CRA program accounts, principally RT for GST/HST, and any required payroll, import-export or information-reporting accounts. 4. Register for QST with Revenu Québec where the partnership is carrying on business in Quebec or is otherwise required to collect QST, including the applicable rules for non-resident and specified digital-service suppliers. 5. Register for import-export privileges with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA), including a RM account where commercial imports or exports require one. 6. Establish electronic filing access, appoint a Canadian or Quebec tax representative where appropriate, and retain records supporting residency, partnership classification, taxable supplies, customer location and export status. A foreign entity does not receive a single Canadian VAT number automatically; the BN, GST/HST account number and QST identification number are separate identifiers.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian limited partnership is generally fiscally transparent for Canadian income-tax purposes: the partnership computes income and allocates it to partners under the Income Tax Act, while partners generally report their allocated shares. Canada has no United States-style check-the-box election for Canadian partnerships. Classification of a foreign partnership for Canadian purposes is determined under Canadian law and relevant treaty principles, not by an automatic elective form. Partnerships may make or participate in specific statutory elections where applicable, including elections concerning allocation, disposition or treatment of partnership property and income, but these do not convert the partnership into a general corporate taxpayer. Canada has enacted hybrid-mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act; no general elective hybrid-mismatch classification election is available. Foreign partners must separately assess Canadian filing, withholding, treaty, permanent-establishment and section 116 or other source-tax obligations.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Federal Goods and Services Tax (GST), harmonized sales tax (HST) in participating provinces, and Quebec Sales Tax (QST). Quebec generally applies 5.000% GST plus 9.975% QST to taxable supplies, producing a standard combined rate of 14.975% where both taxes apply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies, calculated under the applicable small-supplier rules over the prescribed preceding four-quarter period or in the current quarter, is the principal GST/HST registration threshold. Quebec generally uses a CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold for QST purposes, subject to specific rules for non-resident and specified digital-service suppliers. Registration can be required earlier where the business ceases to be a small supplier, voluntarily registers, imports taxable commercial goods, or falls within a special digital-economy or non-resident registration rule. Taxable digital subscriptions and app-based reading access supplied to customers in Canada or Quebec may create collection obligations based on customer-location evidence, contractual supply structure and the role of Apple or Google.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not generally impose a universal real-time e-invoice clearance, government API pre-approval or digital tax-stamp mandate for ordinary GST/HST or QST invoices. Registrants must issue and retain records containing the prescribed supplier identity, applicable GST/HST or QST registration number where required, consideration, tax rate and tax amount, and must retain reliable electronic records for the statutory retention period. CRA and Revenu Québec may accept electronic records if they remain accessible, legible, complete and auditable. GST/HST and QST returns and payments are generally filed electronically where required or where the registrant uses the relevant online portal. CERS electronic export declarations apply to prescribed commercial exports, but they are customs filings rather than VAT-clearance invoices. Apple App Store and Google Play billing may operate as principal, marketplace or payment intermediary depending on contractual facts; the partnership must document whether the platform or the LP is the supplier for indirect-tax purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada may generally be zero-rated for GST/HST when the statutory export conditions are satisfied and the supplier retains evidence that the goods were exported or delivered for export. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated where the specific exported-service rules apply, including the general rule for services supplied to a non-resident and performed in relation to matters outside Canada, subject to exclusions and customer-status requirements. Electronically supplied web-fiction subscriptions, app access and interactive reading services are not automatically zero-rated merely because the supplier is Canadian or payment is received from abroad. The supplier must establish customer location, contractual recipient, place of performance and applicable exclusions. Services supplied to Canadian consumers are generally taxable; QST and GST/HST treatment must be analyzed separately, including specified digital-product and non-resident supplier rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: For exported goods: Canadian Export Declaration filed through the CBSA Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS), where required
Commercial invoice or equivalent accounting document identifying exporter, consignee, description, value, currency, origin and destination
Bill of lading, airway bill, courier record or other carrier evidence showing shipment from Canada to a destination outside Canada
Purchase order, sales contract and delivery terms supporting export eligibility
Proof of delivery, customs import record or foreign receipt where needed to substantiate that the goods left Canada

For exported services or digital supplies: non-resident customer evidence, billing address and payment data, IP or geolocation evidence where relevant, service agreement, usage records, evidence of offshore performance or foreign recipient status, and documentation supporting the applicable zero-rating provision

An inward remittance certificate is not a generally mandatory Canadian GST/HST or QST document; bank payment records may be retained as corroborating evidence but do not independently establish zero-rating
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Canada has no general statutory requirement that export proceeds be repatriated within 180 days. Export zero-rating may be denied or retrospectively assessed where the statutory conditions, customer status, export evidence or service classification are not met. The supplier may become liable for uncollected GST/HST or QST, arrears interest and applicable administrative penalties. False statements, omissions, deliberate tax evasion or fraudulent input-tax-credit or rebate claims may attract civil penalties, including gross-negligence penalties generally calculated by reference to the understated net tax or improperly claimed amount, and criminal prosecution under applicable federal or Quebec law. Customs violations may result in penalties under the Administrative Monetary Penalty System, seizure or forfeiture, reassessment and interest. Voluntary disclosure, correction and documentary remediation should be considered before audit contact where eligibility or filing errors are identified.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) acts as monetary authority and sole issuer of Canadian legal tender, while the Department of Finance Canada and FINTRAC administer the complementary regulatory perimeter under the Currency Act, the Bank of Canada Act, and the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration and issues no FX permits under IMF Article VIII; all current-account and capital-account transactions are free from exchange-control authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts; no approval or quota applies to profit remittance, partnership distributions, or repatriation of non-resident capital. For a Quebec limited partnership (CA_LP) with non-resident partners, the only conversion frictions are tax-driven: (i) a 25% Part XIII withholding tax under the Canadian Income Tax Act applies to Canadian-source amounts allocated or paid to non-resident partners, reducible to treaty rates (e.g., 15% or 5% under Canada-US Article XI, or 0% for literary royalty flows under Article XII of the Canada-US Treaty); (ii) a non-resident partner carrying on business in Canada through the LP is subject to Part I tax on its Canadian-source business income and must file an NR4/T1044 non-resident return; (iii) USD revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing may be retained in a USD concentration account or converted to CAD without any mandatory surrender. For tax measurement in Quebec, USD receipts are translated into CAD at the Bank of Canada noon exchange rate as of the relevant fiscal date; unrealized FX gains on USD cash balances at year-end are recognized as ordinary income under ITA s.39(2) and do not qualify for capital-gains treatment.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory timeline for export-proceeds surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation obligation for digital content receipts. Apple and Google IAP settlement proceeds may be held in USD indefinitely or converted at bank-quoted market rates. The sole reporting requirement is informational: any Qualifying Electronic Fund Transfer (QEFTR) in or out of Canada equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000 in a 24-hour period must be reported by the financial institution to FINTRAC; this reporting does not restrict convertibility or settlement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account + Operational Concentration Account
Operational Account (USD commercial treasury account for IAP sweeps)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer, and similar) are feasible only as secondary collection or vendor-payout utilities and are not viable as the primary clearing rail for a Quebec LP. Legal constraints: (a) only Payments Canada members, being Schedule I/II banks and select credit unions, may clear Canadian-dollar obligations through Lynx (high-value) and ACSS (retail); an EMI holds no Payments Canada clearing membership; (b) EMI balances constitute e-money obligations, not bank deposits, and are not CDIC-insured; (c) a Quebec entity that operates an FX or electronic-funds remittance ledger, including through an offshore EMI, must register as an RSVM (money-services business) with Revenu Quebec and as a money-services business with FINTRAC; failure to register exposes the CA_LP to administrative monetary penalties; (d) routing Apple/Google IAP proceeds through an EMI before a corporate bank account may cause re-characterization as escrow or agent arrangements for GST/QST and FATCA/CRS purposes; (e) incoming USD to an EMI from non-resident partners may trigger additional FINTRAC QEFTR duplication. Feasibility rating: MEDIUM as a collection sweeper and vendor-payout rail, LOW as the sole treasury clearing facade for regulatory resilience.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a newly formed Quebec LP with non-resident partners, all tier-1 Quebec branches require at least one physical appearance of the General Partner (or its authorized signing officer) at a Montreal-area branch to activate the account. Remote video KYC is permitted only for Canadian-resident individual signatories; an entity-level LP account with non-resident partners requires in-person attestation of identity plus two certified documents: (i) the notarized limited partnership agreement, and (ii) a current Registraire des entreprises (NEQ) attestation confirming active LP registration and the filing of beneficial-ownership information. A Canadian counsel-controlled introduction protocol can waive the in-person interview only at the specific credit authorities of the bank's enhanced remote-attestation unit; BMO and NBC have limited waiver discretion, while RBC and TD generally enforce a physical interview for non-resident general-partner structures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident US or OFC-partner majority ownership of the CA_LP capital account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed LP agreement with a capital-commitment schedule; IRS Form W-8BEN-E and FATCA/CRS self-certification (Country of Residence: United States or applicable OFC); Canada Part XIII treaty-relief rider (Form NR301 or RC394); capital-call funding trail evidenced by matched SWIFT MT103 messages; Quebec Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des beneficiaires) filing confirmation from the Registraire des entreprises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large escrow deposit exceeding CAD 250,000 in a single funding sweep
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three months of verified bank statements of the funding partner; certified source-of-wealth declaration executed by the partner; partnership capital and contribution ledger; certified accountant's source-of-funds attestation; criminal and regulatory background check of the General Partner and all authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent round-trip sweeps between Apple/Google IAP settlement accounts and the USD treasury concentration account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apple and Google settlement payout statements for the trailing 12 months; ISIC 9000 / NAICS 511130 business-description certificate; AMF (Autorite des marches financiers) no-licence confirmation letter confirming statutory licensing is not required; six-month revenue projection; compliance-officer sign-off on the digital subscription platform operating model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Missing or stale Quebec beneficial-ownership transparency filing for the LP
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Latest NEQ attestation proving beneficial-owner registration; signed declaration of ultimate beneficial owners; complete records of any nominee, trust, or holding-company arrangements with supporting trust deed; annual renewal receipt from the Registraire des entreprises showing the LP in good standing.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident partners wire capital contributions via SWIFT MT103 to the tier-1 bank's US correspondent (RBC: Bank of New York Mellon; NBC: JPMorgan Chase) with message field 70 structured as 'PURPOSE: CAP. CONTRIB. CA_LP NEQ [registration number]'; funds settle into the LP's CAD operating account through Lynx (high-value) or ACSS (retail). All inward EFTs of CAD 10,000 or more are reported by the bank to FINTRAC as Qualifying EFT Reports; no exchange approval or capital-flow permit is required by Bank of Canada or Finance Canada. Apple IAP and Google Play Billing USD proceeds remit to a segregated USD concentration account at the tier-1 bank; CAD conversion for operating disbursements executes at market rate with a pre-agreed margin (typically below 40 basis points). Capital contributions are GST/QST-neutral when made as pure equity injections without an in-kind asset contribution; no Quebec consumption tax is triggered.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Author and licensor royalties are paid by SWIFT MT103 (gpi-trackable) from the CAD/USD treasury account with payment purpose code 2000 (Royalties); Quebec withholding under ITA s.212 is applied at 25% unless a tax treaty reduces the rate (Canada-US Article XII: 0% for literary copyright royalties on original serialized works; 10% for other patent/know-how rights). Content-infrastructure payments (cloud hosting, translation subcontracting, editorial services) clear through the same MT103 rail or through a commercial letter of credit when the underlying obligation exceeds CAD 50,000; a confirmed sight LC requires a drawdown package comprising the platform revenue statement, partial delivery certificate, and GST/QST invoice from the counterparty to support input tax credit recovery. For recurring small-value obligations (below CAD 50,000), ACSS ACH/EFT settlement suffices. All outbound payments are subject to a corporate-account sweep control to prevent any negative balance on the USD concentration account; surplus USD is swept weekly to the LYNX-enabled CAD operating account at a systematic conversion schedule.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD forward contracts with tenor up to 12 months executed with the tier-1 bank under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex; margin posting triggered only above bank-defined credit thresholds.
Vanilla CAD/USD cross-currency swaps used as cash-flow hedges against the USD-denominated Apple/Google IAP receivable pool.
FX collar and zero-cost option structures on forecast quarterly Apple/Google settlement flows to cap conversion cost without speculative premium outlay.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible but commercially non-standard for CAD because the currency is fully deliverable; an NDF may be used only for residual exposure outside CAD settlement rails and must be designated as a hedge under IFRS 9 to preserve the LP's pass-through tax status and avoid re-characterization as a financial institution under ITA s.149.1.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration Annuelle) under An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (Québec)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after the anniversary of the LP’s date of initial registration; almanac date is not a fixed fiscal year but contractually set to each anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing monetary penalty of CAD 15 per month up to CAD 150; continued failure triggers administrative dissolution of the declaration record and may result in the partnership being struck off the register and prohibited from operating

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (including allocation of income and expenses to each partner)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and, for Quebec residents, Revenu Québec (TP-600 equivalent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due no later than March 31 following the end of the calendar fiscal year; if the LP’s fiscal year is not December 31, the deadline is the last day of the third month following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 100 per day with a minimum penalty of CAD 100 for deliberate non-filing; principal partners may be assessed additional penalties for unreported allocations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual registration update and confirmation of beneficial owners (registre des bénéficiaires ultimes) integrated into the Quebec Annual Declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same anniversary deadline as the Annual Declaration; any change in limited partners owning 25% or more must be reported within 30 days of the change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to report ultimate beneficial owners may lead to an immediate blockage of the annual declaration and the issuance of compulsory conformity notices with penalties up to CAD 5,000; knowingly false statements may attract disqualification and court orders

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory independent audit is required for a Quebec limited partnership solely by reason of partner liability; an audited financial statement becomes compulsory only if (i) expressly required by the partnership agreement, (ii) mandated by Revenu Québec or the CRA through a written notification, or (iii) the LP is a registered securities issuer under securities legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for publicly accountable partnerships; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) for private partnerships in Canada; Quebec LSA requires registered enterprises to maintain accounting records sufficient to prove their activity and to support annual filings

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the general partner must confirm the list of all partners holding 25% or more of capital voting rights, and identify each ultimate beneficial owner of such partners, through the Registraire des entreprises' UBO portal. Changes in ownership of 25% or more must be filed within 30 days of the transaction. The UBO declaration is an integral part of the Annual Declaration and cannot be omitted.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partner Interests (ownership and contributions)
Register of General Partners (management and indemnity provisions)
Minute Book and Resolutions of the General Partner
Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (when applicable, mirroring REQ filing)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – 1,200 per year for a professional registered office in Quebec (Montreal-based virtual office plus annual agent service)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 – 8,000 per year for a full independent audit of a small-to-medium webnovel subscription platform; USD 1,200 – 3,000 for a review engagement (non-statutory)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal and Quebec headline corporate rate (15% federal general rate + 11.5% Quebec general rate) for taxable corporations; the CA_LP is a limited partnership and is fiscally transparent, so the partnership itself is not subject to entity-level corporate income tax.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No entity-level incentive applies to the LP itself. At the partner level, eligible expenditures may benefit from SR&ED federal refundable investment tax credits (25%/37.5%) and the Quebec Innovation Tax Credit (30%) for software and digital-content development; the Quebec QST rebate for digital production and audiovisual services can reduce tax on production costs; if the corporate general partner is a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC), the small business deduction on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income yields a combined federal/Quebec rate of approximately 12.2%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: Form T5013 – Statement of Partnership Income and T5013 Summary (Canada Revenue Agency, online via XML Internet File Transfer within CRA My Business Account). Quebec: Revenu Québec Form CO-1029 – Partnership Information Return (Société de personnes) filed through the CLIC portal, supplemented by Relevé 15 slips for each partner.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal period elected by the partnership; must generally conform to the taxation year of all major partners unless a different period is approved by CRA).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than 5 months after the end of the partnership fiscal period (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 year-end); Revenu Québec applies the same federal deadline for the CO-1029 return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the date on which the partnership's Canadian fiscal period ends; for non-resident partners, the date must be the same as the period used to compute Canadian-source income allocated to those partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership statutory address and province of establishment (Quebec for QST).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LP has no office in Quebec but carries on business through a permanent establishment in Quebec, provide the address of the Canadian agent for service and identify the permanent establishment location.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross digital subscription revenues, including in-app purchase revenue from Apple App Store and Google Play Billing, advertising income, and serialized content licensing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Canadian-source gross revenue from Quebec users, apps, subscribers, and advertisers. Where the non-resident LP is considered to carry on business in Canada, file under Part I on a net-basis return; otherwise no Canadian revenue should be reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Platform operating expenses: content author payments, app store commissions, hosting, software development, amortization of capitalized development, and Quebec R&D expenditures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate expenses directly related to earning Canadian-source income; maintain contemporaneous records linking each expense to the Canadian subscription platform, especially app-store commission charges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of net income/loss to partners, distinguishing capital allocation, taxable allocation, and guaranteed payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each non-resident partner, enter the agreed income allocation in accordance with the LP agreement and Canadian allocation rules; a non-resident partner receiving an allocation of Canadian-source business income is required to file a Canadian T1 or T2 return and report that amount unless granted relief under a tax treaty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of T5013/CO-1029: federal penalty under s.162(7) of CAD 100 per day (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500), plus an additional per-partner late-filing penalty of CAD 100 per month for partnerships with more than five partners; Revenu Québec imposes a similar CAD 50 per day penalty up to CAD 2,500 plus CAD 500 per missing or late Relevé 15 slip; failure to file within statute may also trigger reassessment and loss of entitlement to certain deductions.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII gross dividend withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to non-resident shareholders. The limited partnership itself makes no dividend withholding because it is pass-through; however, distributions of Canadian-source business profits to non-resident partners are taxed under Part I on a net-basis unless exempted or reduced by tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A non-resident partner claiming treaty benefits must file a valid Canadian income tax return (T1 for individuals, T2 for corporations), attach a completed Form NR301 – Declaration of Eligibility for Benefits Under a Tax Treaty and, where required, a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the partner's tax authority; for Quebec, the Relevé 15 and supporting documentation must be provided to Revenu Québec, which may require a treaty-protected Quebec return where the LP has a Quebec permanent establishment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII WHT is 25% for both patent/royalty income and interest paid to non-residents; however, Canada exempts most arm's-length interest from withholding under s.212(3)(b) where the debt is made in the ordinary course of business or is payable on a long-term debt of a specified issuer. Under the Canada–US treaty, royalties for software/online-content copyright are generally 0%, and interest is 0% where the beneficial owner is not exempted by domestic rules; under the Canada–UK and Canada–France treaties, copyright royalties are typically 0% or 10%, and other industrial royalties are 10%, with interest 0% or 10% depending on the recipient and treaty provisions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Form T106 (Information Return on Transactions with Non-Residents) is mandatory when the aggregate value of transactions between the partnership and a non-arm's length non-resident exceeds CAD 1,000,000 in a taxation year; CRA also expects contemporaneous Local File/Master File documentation for taxpayers with gross revenue of at least CAD 50,000,000 or assets of CAD 250,000,000, and country-by-country reporting (CbCR) applies to multinational groups with consolidated revenue exceeding CAD 1,000,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada and Quebec have no stand-alone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) as seen in offshore financial centres. However, the Income Tax Act section 245 (General Anti-Avoidance Rule) and Quebec's Tax Administration Act section 53 apply a substance-over-form doctrine; CRA and Revenu Québec will disregard artificial filing structures where the LP lacks real employees, physical presence, decision-making authority, and genuine economic risk in Quebec, especially where revenue from Apple/Google digital sales is diverted to a shell foreign entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Wilful Blindness (Digital Revenue Suppression)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to record or report revenue from Apple IAP and Google Play Billing, routing subscription proceeds through a non-substantive offshore clearing company, creating fictitious content-licencing deductions, or using a nominee partner to conceal Canadian-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA gross-negligence penalty under s.163(2) of 50% of the understated tax plus arrears interest; criminal prosecution under s.239(1) of the Income Tax Act is punishable by a fine of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to 5 years; Revenu Québec can impose an additional 50% penalty under the Tax Administration Act and seize assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the corporate general partner are personally and severally liable under s.227.1 ITA and section 103 of the Quebec Tax Administration Act for unremitted source deductions, QST, and Part XIII withholdings; where evasion is proven, courts may pierce the corporate veil, order civil restitution to CRA/Revenu Québec, issue travel bans under CRA's international enforcement program, and impose imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Statutory Filing Failure / Non-resident Partner Oversight
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the T5013 and CO-1029 partnership information returns, failing to issue Relevé 15 slips to non-resident partners, under-declaring partnership allocations, or incorrectly allowing a non-resident partner to avoid Canadian tax by not filing a Part I return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalties of CAD 100 per day to a maximum of CAD 2,500 plus per-slip penalties of CAD 500 for each missing Relevé 15; the partnership may lose the ability to claim expenses or be denied allocation of losses to partners; a non-resident partner who fails to file is subject to the gross-negligence penalty and, for repeated non-compliance, criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner who approved or participated in causing false filings are jointly and severally liable for all unpaid amounts deemed withheld or required to be reported; the deregistration of the LP does not extinguish director liability, and CRA may issue a federal lien or Revenu Québec a legal mortgage over personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing / Profit Shifting without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying a non-arm's length foreign group company an excessive royalty or service fee for the WebNovel platform, signing false intercompany contracts without local employees or functions, failing to prepare Form T106, or misallocated hard-to-value intangible valuation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA reassesses to arm's length prices under s.247(2), adds a 10% transfer-pricing penalty under s.247(3), and charges prescribed-rate interest compounded daily; expenses may be disallowed outright, and redirected amounts to a foreign parent company may be recharacterized as a taxable dividend subject to 25% Part XIII withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or transmit false transfer-pricing documentation are exposed to gross-negligence penalties under s.163.2; in egregious cases CRA can assess directors jointly and severally for the foreign parent's Canadian tax liability on the basis of de facto control and piercing the corporate veil, and obtain seizure orders against personal bank accounts and real property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Shell Company and Beneficial Ownership Red Flags
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the LP with a nominee general partner and undisclosed foreign beneficial owner, receiving Apple/Google payouts into accounts in non-cooperative jurisdictions without business purpose, failing to maintain a Quebec register of beneficial owners under the Quebec Business Companies Act, or conducting subscription volume inconsistent with source-region content.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Pursuant to the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLFTA), the entity can be assessed monetary penalties up to CAD 500,000 for failure to maintain required records; provincial beneficial-ownership violations carry up to CAD 100,000 fines; tax-return disallowance may follow where the true economic owner cannot be demonstrated; in criminal calibrations, digital assets and revenue flows may be restrained or forfeited.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the general partner may be personally liable for penalties and restitution where the LP is found to be a facade for money laundering; a criminal conviction under the Criminal Code for laundering proceeds of crime carries imprisonment up to 10 years; travel bans and asset freezes are regularly issued in multi-jurisdictional extradition proceedings; corporate-veil protection is completely inapplicable to illegal activity.
